function: GE-MAPDQN multi-agent RL jointly sets UAV trajectory, task association, sub-carrier allocation and power allocation for communication users and sensing vehicles of OFDM ISAC UAVs (p. 7).
system: 3 UAVs, OFDM ISAC (10 sub-carriers, 0.25 MHz, 40 dBm), 30 users, 3 sensing vehicles; antennas and band not stated; no RIS (pp. 3, 12).
method: GE-MAPDQN: multi-agent parametrized deep Q-network (actor-critic for continuous actions, DQN for discrete), centralized training with decentralized execution, plus game-based action adjuster; reinforcement learning (pp. 6-11).
data_channel: Own simulator: probabilistic LoS air-to-ground channel and radar echo model; 500x500 m area, 30 random users, 3 sensing vehicles; no dataset or measurements (pp. 4-5, 12).
test_conditions: Online training in one scenario (3 UAVs, 30 users, 3 vehicles); user distribution and vehicle mobility change at slot 3000 and the networks are retrained (pp. 11-13).
baselines: Non-learned: random MA-TRC scheme. Learned: MADDPG, MAPPO, single-agent PDQN (SAPDQN); variants without the game adjuster (MAPDQN), with random trajectory or random task schedule (p. 12).
metrics: Accumulated reward (weighted data rate plus radar estimation rate minus penalties), weighted rate, delay-Doppler CRLB, UAV trajectories (pp. 6, 12-14).
complexity: Analytic orders: training O(Tfwd+Tbwd) from layer sizes; inference O(sum W Nmax^2) + O(w1MN) + O(w2N^3+w2NlogN); no runtime measured (pp. 11-13).
q1_support: p. 4: "We adopt a common probabilistic LoS model to describe the air-to-ground data transmission links" (own air-to-ground and radar-echo models; no 3GPP TR 38.811 or measured data is mentioned).
q2_support: p. 13: "we change the user distribution and the sensing vehicle mobilities at time slot 3000" (performance drops, then recovers after online retraining of the networks with new experience tuples, pp. 11, 13).
q3_support: p. 12: "Random: UAVs randomly chooses its MA-TRC scheme" is the non-learned baseline; MADDPG, MAPPO and SAPDQN are the learned baselines, compared on weighted rate, CRLB and reward in Figs. 5-6 (p. 13).
q4_support: p. 11: "The computational complexity of the proposed GE-MAPDQN algorithm mainly comes from two parts" (training and inference orders, eqs. 45-48, pp. 11-13).
q5_support: p. 12: "UAVs fly around to provide ISAC service for" (self-built simulated scenario; no code or data link, no public or measured dataset).
notes: Area 6 over 5 by precedence: learned power, sub-carrier, trajectory and association decisions for UAV aerial links that also sense (pp. 6-7); ISAC would also fit. Passes above_phy because power and sub-carrier allocation on aerial links are learned jointly with trajectory and association. The antenna configuration is never stated, and area 6 admits single-antenna links. The game-based adjuster (coalition formation, cost sharing with Hungarian and water-filling) is not learned and runs inside the loop (p. 10). Borderline q2: adaptation is online retraining after the change at slot 3000 (pp. 11, 13), the amount of new data is not stated.
